# Phase 2 review fixes (still release 1.54.0; amend the existing 1.54.0 CHANGELOG section, no version bump)

## 1. Router: cheap lanes first, Claude only after 2 real failures

In tools/router.mjs:

- Export `CHEAP_ORDER = Object.freeze(['hermes', 'cursor', 'codex', 'openrouter'])`. Keep `ROUTE_ORDER` exported and unchanged.
- Cheap candidate order for a job: the job's `typeRoute` entries (in order, skipping `claude`), then every `CHEAP_ORDER` lane not already listed. A job without `typeRoute` uses `CHEAP_ORDER`.
- Filter cheap candidates: lane must have a configured model; `openrouter` only when `job.sensitive === false` (see 2); `accepts(...)` must not return false; drop any lane with `failures[lane] >= 2`.
- `tier: "expensive"`: unchanged, Claude only (reason `tier expensive`).
- If any cheap candidate remains: return the first one whose health is not `paused` (reason `cheapest healthy lane`, or `fallback after 2 failures on <lanes>` when some lane was dropped for failures). If every remaining cheap candidate is paused, return the first one with reason `...; lane <x> paused` so the job waits for it. Never jump to Claude because cheap lanes are paused.
- If no cheap candidate remains: return Claude only when Claude has a configured model, is accepted, `failures.claude < 2`, and the cheap lanes together have at least 2 real failures (sum of `failures` over cheap lanes >= 2). Reason `fallback after 2 failures on <comma-separated failed lanes>`.
- Otherwise throw `route-exhausted` (code `route-exhausted`). When no cheap lane is configured at all and nothing failed, the message must say: `route-exhausted: no cheap lane available for job <id>; Claude needs 2 real failures first or tier "expensive"`.
- "Real failures" are what the runner already counts in `routeFailures` (failed/timeout only; rate limits and quota pauses never count). Do not change that counting.

In tools/job-types.mjs: remove `claude` from preset routes (merge becomes `['codex']`, lead becomes `['codex']`). Everything else unchanged.

Tests (tests/router.test.mjs), at least:
- docs job (`typeRoute: ['hermes']`), all lanes configured, Hermes paused: routes to hermes with a paused reason, never Claude.
- docs job, Hermes not configured: routes to cursor (next cheap lane), not Claude.
- docs job, every cheap lane paused: waits on hermes.
- Claude chosen only after cheap lanes collected 2 real failures and no cheap lane is left; one failure is not enough.
- only Claude configured, no failures: `route-exhausted` with the message above.
- typeRoute order respected then the cheap order (e.g. test type `['codex','cursor']` with codex failed twice goes to cursor, then hermes, ...).
Update existing router/lanes/lanes-run tests whose expectations relied on the old Claude fallback, keeping their intent (e.g. an OpenRouter→Claude fallback test now needs `sensitive: false` and 2 real failures).

## 2. Sensitive by default

- A job is sensitive unless it sets `sensitive: false`. Missing `sensitive` means sensitive.
- tools/router.mjs: openrouter is a cheap candidate only when `job.sensitive === false`.
- tools/swarm.mjs validateManifest: an explicit `agent: "openrouter"` job without `sensitive: false` refuses with code `sensitive-openrouter`, message `Job <id>: OpenRouter only gets jobs that set sensitive: false`. Keep the existing boolean type check.
- Update every existing test fixture that uses an explicit openrouter agent (and expects it to validate or run) to set `sensitive: false`. Do not weaken assertions.
- Tests: an auto job with no `sensitive` and only hermes paused + openrouter configured never routes to openrouter; an auto job with `sensitive: false` can; explicit openrouter without the field refuses with `sensitive-openrouter`; with `sensitive: false` it validates.

## 3. Docs write rule

tools/job-types.mjs `isDocsFile(relPath)`:
- Normalize backslashes to `/`.
- Refuse anything under `docs/state/` (prefix match, case-insensitive).
- Doc extensions: `.md`, `.mdx`, `.rst`, `.adoc` (case-insensitive). A path anywhere with one of these is a docs file.
- `.txt` is not a doc extension, except the allowlisted basenames `README.txt` and `CHANGELOG.txt` (exact basename, case-insensitive), in any directory.
- Under `docs/`, a file still needs a doc extension (or allowlisted basename); `docs/x.js`, `docs/data.json` are not docs files.
Tests (tests/job-types.test.mjs): `requirements.txt` false, `docs/x.js` false, `docs/data.json` false, `docs/state/usage-ledger.md` false, `README.txt` and `notes/CHANGELOG.txt` true, `guide.txt` false, `docs/guide.md` true, `guide.adoc` true. Update the existing isDocsFile test to match.
